newsitem.title: USA: TI wins $1 bln royalty deal from Samsung.
newsitem.headline: TI wins $1 bln royalty deal from Samsung.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc said Tuesday it has reached agreement with Samsung Electronics Co Ltd on a 10-year cross-licensing deal that it expects will result in more than $1 billion in royalties.
In a statement, Texas Instruments said the deal replaces a previous five year deal that expired at the end of 1995 and settles all pending litigation between the two companies.
The company said that it expects to accrue about $105 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 for "catch-up royalties" covering the first nine months of 1996.

The new cross-license deal, which runs until the end of 2005, covers a broad base of patents, including those for semiconductors, personal computers, consumer products and telecommunications equipment, it said.
With this deal, Texas Instruments said it has almost completed its 1995 round of patent cross-license agreements with the major semiconductor makers.
Earlier in the year, TI reached 10-year deals with Fujitsu Ltd, Oki Electric Industry Co Ltd and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd.
It said talks continue with NEC Corp and several smaller firms.
